exercise.name: Barbell Reverse Grip Incline Bench Row

reference.title: Barbell Reverse Grip Incline Bench Row
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the bar comes up, in as it lowers; the pad lets you breathe freely.
breathing.cadence: About 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 2 s down
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: the chest stays on the pad, about 2 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches the pad with a pause.

cues.text: Set the bench to about 40 degrees, chest on the pad, chin over the top, feet planted behind; underhand grip about shoulder width, arms hanging.
Drive the elbows back close to the sides and pull the bar up toward the pad.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for a moment; the chest stays on the pad.
Arms long, chest on the pad, repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest down; lighten the bar.
Think of driving the elbows back; the hands are hooks.
Pull the shoulder blades back and down, not up.
Straighten the arms fully at the bottom.

kinematics.norm: Chest-supported rows remove most of the lower-back load of a bent-over row (Fenwick 2009)
Underhand grip keeps the elbows close and brings in the biceps (Lehman 2004)
The chest stays on the pad; only the arms and shoulder blades move (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Lock the bench angle and make sure the bench is stable before loading.
Elbow or biceps pain with the underhand grip: use an overhand or neutral grip.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shorter range if the bar meets the bench early.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Drive the elbows back close to the body; the underhand grip keeps the arm path close (Lehman 2004).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Drive the elbows back close to the body; the underhand grip keeps the arm path close (Lehman 2004).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Elbow flexor, working harder with the palms up.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Elbow flexor, working harder with the palms up.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Extends the shoulder behind the trunk.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Extends the shoulder behind the trunk.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the chest on the pad.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk long; the pad takes most of the load off the back.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk long; the pad takes most of the load off the back.
muscleNotes.quads_r: The legs brace against the floor to keep the chest on the pad.
muscleNotes.quads_l: The legs brace against the floor to keep the chest on the pad.
